pages.name: One pin
pages.text: A pin at (2, 5) lets the line swing to any tilt, leaving a fan of lines it could be. Set `m = 3` and the fan closes to one line, `y = 3x + c`. The pin must fit that rule, so put its x and y in, [[substituting]] them, and solve for c.

pages.name: Through a point
pages.task: A line goes through (1, 4) with gradient 2. Which is its rule?
pages.why: The gradient is 2, so the rule is `y = 2x + c`. Put (1, 4) in: `4 = 2 × 1 + c`, so `4 = 2 + c`, and `c = 4 − 2 = 2`. The rule is `y = 2x + 2`.

pages.name: Keep the minus
pages.task: A line goes through (2, −1) with gradient −3. Which is its rule?
pages.why: The gradient is −3, so `y = −3x + c`. Put (2, −1) in: `−1 = −3 × 2 + c`, so `−1 = −6 + c`, and `c = −1 + 6 = 5`. The rule is `y = −3x + 5`.

pages.name: Mind the brackets
pages.why: `m = (7 − 1) ÷ (1 − (−2)) = 6 ÷ 3 = 2`. Either point works, and (1, 7) has no minus signs, so it is the easier one to put in: `7 = 2 × 1 + c`, so `7 = 2 + c`, and `c = 5`. The rule is `y = 2x + 5`, and (−2, 1) checks: `2 × (−2) + 5 = 1`.

pages.name: Parallel
pages.task: Which line is parallel to `y = −3x + 4` and goes through (1, 5)?
pages.why: A parallel line keeps `m = −3`, so `y = −3x + c`. Put (1, 5) in: `5 = −3 × 1 + c`, so `5 = −3 + c`, and `c = 5 + 3 = 8`. The rule is `y = −3x + 8`.
